tagline: A shared team inbox with internal comments and assignment
verdictSummary: A shared team inbox — multiple people seeing the same set of incoming emails, leaving internal comments, assigning who handles what — is a real weekend-to-week build on top of a connected mailbox. What doesn't survive: Missive's polish across many channels beyond email (SMS, social DMs), and years of team-workflow refinement around assignment and internal discussion.
coreLoopDIY: Connect one shared mailbox via IMAP/SMTP, let multiple team members view the same inbox, leave internal comments on a message thread, and assign a message to a specific teammate.
whatYouLose: a unified inbox across channels beyond email, like SMS or social
shared contact and conversation history across the whole team
rules and automation for routing incoming messages
whyPeopleStillPay: A shared inbox view is buildable; making assignment, internal discussion, and cross-channel unification feel effortless for a whole team, every day, is the ongoing product work.
prompt: Build a shared team email inbox: connect one shared mailbox, and let multiple logged-in team members view the same incoming messages, leave internal comments visible only to the team and never sent to the customer, and assign a message to a specific teammate as the owner. Use Next.js/TypeScript with Postgres, and IMAP/SMTP for the connected mailbox — an app-specific password is enough, no OAuth app needed for a single shared mailbox. Sync incoming mail into a shared thread view; each thread shows the message history plus an internal comment thread beneath it, visible only to logged-in team members. Implement assignment (one owner per thread at a time, reassignable) and a simple status per thread (open/done) so the team can see what's been handled. Replying to a customer sends a real email through the connected SMTP account, clearly visually distinct from an internal comment so nobody accidentally sends a private note externally. Add a simple activity log per thread — who commented, assigned, or replied, and when. Do not build support for channels beyond email, automated routing rules, or cross-team contact history — those are out of scope; this is a shared inbox for one mailbox and one small team. Requires hosting, a domain, and the mailbox credentials for the shared account you're connecting.

faq.q: Can it unify email with SMS or social DMs like Missive?
faq.a: No — this build is email only. Unifying multiple channels into one inbox is real, ongoing integration work each channel adds separately.

faq.q: How does the team know who's handling which email?
faq.a: Each thread has one assignable owner and an open/done status, visible to everyone — the same core mechanic Missive uses, just without its deeper workflow refinements.

faq.q: Could I accidentally send an internal comment to the customer?
faq.a: The prompt calls for making internal comments visually distinct from real replies specifically to reduce that risk, but it's still worth double-checking before sending anything — there's no hard technical barrier beyond the UI difference.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting, a domain, and the mailbox you're already paying for — no per-seat fee, unlike Missive's per-user pricing.
